title: Indian Railways Launches a Special Drive for Cleaning and Disinfection of Drinking Water Tanks and Filters
subtitle: Zonal Railways Advised to Undertake Comprehensive Inspection and Rectification of Drinking-Water Infrastructure; Station-Wise Deficiencies and Action Taken to be Monitored
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 AUG 2026 11:37AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian Railways has launched a special cleanliness drive across the railway network focused on cleaning and disinfection of drinking-water tanks and filtration systems to ensure the continued availability of safe and clean drinking water for passengers at railway stations.
The initiative is part of a broader action plan for strengthening drinking-water quality management across Indian Railways. The action plan emphasises frequent inspection and maintenance of the entire drinking-water system, along with water-quality testing at the source as well as at the point of consumption, rather than relying solely on end-of-pipe water testing.
During the drive, Zonal Railways will undertake comprehensive inspection of water sources, treatment and filtration plants, underground and overhead tanks, PVC tanks, water booths, taps and water dispensing points. All drinking-water tanks will be drained, desludged, scrubbed and disinfected. Measures will also be taken to ensure tight covers and appropriate protection of vents and overflow points from birds, animals and algae.
The drive will also identify deficiencies requiring corrective action. Damaged tanks, pipelines and filters will be repaired or replaced, wherever required, while ensuring that there is no cross-connection between potable and non-potable water systems. All piping forming part of the drinking-water circuit will also be checked for leakages and necessary corrective measures taken to prevent water wastage.
Special attention will be given to locations where hand pumps and borewells are being used for extraction of drinking water. Zonal Railways will ensure that water from such systems remains free from contamination and is safe for potable use.
Strengthening Water Quality Management
As part of the broader action plan, the Railway Board has advised Zonal Railways to undertake comprehensive inspection of water coolers and water purification systems. Water tanks in coolers will be thoroughly cleaned, leakages in coolers, pipelines and taps will be addressed promptly, and 100 per cent hygiene around water-cooler dispensing areas will be ensured.
UV/RO purification systems for water coolers will be checked for proper functioning and provided wherever required. Scheduled maintenance, servicing, overhauling and timely replacement of filter candles and other components will be undertaken wherever due. New or replacement UV/RO systems, based on their condition and requirement, are also to be taken up in mission mode.
The prescribed measures for cleaning, purification and quality monitoring will also be applicable to Water Vending Machines to ensure that drinking water dispensed through such facilities meets the required safety and hygiene standards.
The officials will undertake physical, chemical and bacteriological testing of water samples from identified locations, including sources, post-treatment outlets, tanks, coolers, vending machines and representative taps or booths, wherever feasible. Daily residual-chlorine monitoring will also be undertaken, with immediate re-chlorination or other corrective action wherever required.
Monitoring of Infrastructure and Corrective Action
Railway Board has directed Zonal Railways to monitor and expedite works already sanctioned for replacement and construction of new overhead and underground tanks. A summary of these sanctioned works will also be prepared, and fresh sanctions, wherever required, will be processed.
Suitable filtration and purification systems for different situations, including at-source and at-tap filtration, are also being worked out to identify and prevent contamination at various stages of the drinking-water supply chain.
Zonal Railways will submit station-wise details of deficiencies identified and the corrective action taken. This mechanism will facilitate systematic monitoring of deficiencies and ensure that issues identified during the special drive are addressed in a time-bound manner.
The action plan also envisages similar measures for drinking-water infrastructure in Railway colonies and workplaces, thereby extending the focus on safe and hygienic drinking water beyond passenger areas.
Through these coordinated measures, Indian Railways is strengthening preventive inspection, infrastructure maintenance, cleaning and disinfection, water-quality testing and corrective-action mechanisms across the drinking-water supply system. The initiative aims to ensure the continued availability of safe, clean and hygienic drinking water for passengers as well as Railway personnel.

title: Regional Manthan Conference on Road Safety
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 AUG 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) today organised a Regional Manthan Conference to deliberate on strengthening road safety through e-Enforcement, integrated data systems, safer vehicles, improved emergency response and stronger district-level capacity for western states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and Union Territory of Dadra Nagar Haveli and Daman Diu (DNH & DD) at Mumbai under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Justice A M Sapre [Retd.], Chairman Supreme Court  Committee on Road Safety. Shri Sanjay Bandyopadhyay Member SCCORS and Shri Mahmood Ahmed AS(T), MoRTH along with other senior officials also attended the conference. The following were deliberated in detail during conference: -
Zero Fatality District Initiative: Targeting Where It Matters Most
Good intentions and good schemes must be directed with precision. The
Zero Fatality District (ZFD) initiative
is our strategic response to the question: where do we act first, and how do we act comprehensively? The ZFD model has been expanded nationally, with
100 critical districts identified across 15 states
for focused, 360-degree intervention combining engineering, enforcement, emergency care, and education. These 100 districts together recorded with an
average of 400+ fatalities per district annually
. The ZFD framework, tailored to each district's specific crash profile, offers a proven strategy to achieve substantial fatality reduction.
B.        PM Rahat: No Victim Should Be Lost for Want of Care
Research tells us that
50% of fatalities can be averted if the victim is admitted to hospital within the first one hour
i.e., the Golden Hour. And yet, across our country, victims lie unattended, families scramble for cash, and hospitals hesitate to act without assurance of payment. The
PM Rahat Scheme
, is our definitive response to this tragedy.
PM Rahat provides
cashless treatment of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for up to 7 days
from the date of accident, covering all road accident victims irrespective of insurance status. What makes this scheme genuinely transformative is its technology backbone including the seamless integration of
eDAR (MoRTH) with TMS 2.0 (NHA)
, the linkage with the
112 emergency helpline
. For the first time, Transport, Health, and Police are working from the same data, in real time, toward the same outcome i.e., no victim is lost due to a delay in care.
C.        Rah-Veer: Honoring the Courage of the Good Samaritan
Even the best emergency care system cannot function if no one acts in those first critical moments at the scene of an accident. This is where the
Rah-Veer scheme
enters. Rah-Veer is the Government of India's formal recognition and reward for Good Samaritans i.e., individuals who, in the face of uncertainty and risk, choose to stop and save a life by rushing the accident victim to hospital within the Golden Hour.
Every Rah-Veer who saves a life in a serious accident including one involving major surgery, brain or spinal cord injury, at least three days of hospitalization, or death during treatment, is entitled to a
cash award of Rs. 25,000 per incident
, accompanied by a Certificate of Appreciation. Critically, these Good Samaritans are also protected by law i.e., no Rah-Veer can be subjected to legal proceedings without their consent.
Together, PM Rahat and Rah-Veer create a complete emergency care chain i.e., from the moment of accident to the moment of full recovery.
D.        Sadak Suraksha Mitra: Building a Community of Road Safety Champions
Road accident statistics reveal that individuals in the age group of 18–45 years account for 66.1% of all fatalities, underscoring the urgent need to involve youth in road safety initiatives. With this objective, the Sadak Suraksha Mitra (SSM) Programme was launched as a youth-led road safety initiative jointly conceptualised by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports.
The programme seeks to strengthen district-level road safety interventions by engaging trained youth volunteers through the MYBharat platform, with a special focus on the top 100 high-fatality districts across the country, where District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) serve as the primary governance mechanism. These volunteers are not passive bystanders; they are structured road safety professionals, assuming defined roles as Crash Scene Coordinators, data collection for Road Safety Auditors, and Awareness & Engagement Leads. Each role contributes to a specific dimension of district-level road safety action, thereby creating a cadre of youth leaders dedicated to reducing fatalities and promoting safer roads.
E.        Data-Driven Hyperlocal Interventions: The Science Behind the Solution
Knowing where accidents happen is only the first step. Acting on that knowledge systematically, at scale, and with the right tools is the harder challenge. The
Data-Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI)
framework, is built precisely for this purpose. DDHI empowers District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) to move from intuition-based planning to evidence-based action.
The DDHI roadmap follows a structured five-stage cycle:
Alignment Meeting, Capacity Building, Interventions Planning, Implementation, and Impact Assessment
. Each district begins with an alignment on programme objectives, moves through capacity building that deskills processes and upskills people, and proceeds to the identification and implementation of hyperlocal interventions suited to that district's unique crash profile.
These five programmes are not just isolated efforts. They are
interlocking pieces of a single, coherent road safety architecture
. Community engagement through SSM feeds into district planning, data intelligence directs enforcement and engineering, Good Samaritans bridge the gap to emergency care and cashless treatment ensures that no Golden Hour is wasted. Hence, every State and district official were urged to take the insights of this workshop back to the field, and integrate these programmes into your road safety plans.
The Conference reaffirmed that reducing road fatalities requires coordinated action across technology, enforcement, vehicle safety, emergency care, crash investigation and institutional capacity.
States and districts were urged to translate these discussions into time-bound action on the ground, strengthening enforcement and road safety systems towards the goal of safer roads and Zero Fatality Districts.
At the end of the conference, it was agreed that States will due root cause analysis of road fatalities, prepare action plan to reduce road accidents and fatalities, prepare District Road Safety Plan to achieve India’s goal of reducing road fatalities by 50% by 2030.
*****

Prof. Manoranjan Parida, Professor, IIT Roorkee, and Prof. Rabibrata Mukherjee, National Coordinator, SPARC, also addressed the gathering. The inaugural address was delivered by Chief Guest Shri Rajesh Verma, IAS, Chairperson, CAQM. The session concluded with the felicitation of the Chief Guest and dignitaries and a vote of thanks by Dr. Pradeep Kumar, Scientist ‘G’ and Head, Pavement Evaluation Division, CSIR-CRRI.
The workshop highlighted that road networks constitute critical public assets and their systematic management is essential for ensuring safe, efficient and cost-effective mobility. The deliberations focused on strengthening scientific and data-driven approaches to road asset management, particularly for improving pavement maintenance decisions and optimising whole-life costs.
The technical programme featured keynote lectures by Prof. Manoranjan Parida and Dr. N. C. Pal, followed by sessions covering road asset management in practice, case studies and implementation challenges; industry perspectives and technologies for road asset management; data acquisition and whole-life costing for road networks, with contributions from Sh. Anukul Saxena, Dr. Bhavesh Jain, Sh.Rohit Mane, Mrs. Prerna Kalra, Dr. Anand Sreeram, Sh. Neeraj Chadha, and Prof. Indrajit Ghosh.
A key highlight of the workshop was the demonstration of the Life-Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA) Tool for Indian Roads, presented by Prof. Kranthi Kumar Kuna and Sh. Soumyarup Biswas. The demonstration provided an opportunity for participants to understand the application of life-cycle cost considerations in road infrastructure decision-making.
The programme concluded with a panel discussion on “From Pilot to Practice: What Will It Take to Make RAMS a Routine Part of Road Agency Decision-Making?”, bringing together experts from academia, government and industry to discuss pathways for wider adoption and institutionalisation of Road Asset Management Systems;
featuring Sh. L. P. Padhy, Prof. S. S. Mohapatra, Prof. Amit Goel, Prof. Nikhil Sabu, Sh. Sunil Jain, and Prof. A. K. Singh.
The workshop provided a valuable platform for knowledge exchange and collaboration among stakeholders and underscored the importance of integrating asset management, predictive analytics, data acquisition and whole-life costing into road infrastructure planning and management. The event concluded with a closing ceremony at CSIR-CRRI.

title: National Conclave on Tribal Languages & Museums begins in Mysuru, Karnataka
subtitle:
Launch of Adi Vaani Platform along with iOS application, addition of five new languages

MoTA AI bot “Jago” Launched

Ministry of Tribal Affairs signs MoU with Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 AUG 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs today began the three-day National Conclave on Tribal Languages & Museums in Mysuru, Karnataka. The Conclave brings together policymakers, linguists, researchers, technologists, and tribal community representatives to deliberate on the documentation and revitalisation of tribal languages and on strengthening tribal and Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums (TFFM) across the country.
The inaugural session was attended by
Shri Durga Das Uikey, Hon'ble Union Minister of State, Ministry of Tribal Affairs
;
Sri Raghumurthy, Hon'ble Minister, Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka
; Shri Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Hon'ble Member of Parliament, Mysuru Constituency; Shri Anant Prakash Pandey, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs; Smt. Kanagavalli, IAS, Secretary, Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka; Prof. Basavaraja Kodagunti, Director, Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL), along with senior officials of the Central and State Governments. The proceedings began with the National Song, the National Anthem and the Naadageethe, followed by the lighting of the ceremonial lamp.
India is witnessing a transformative era in tribal development under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Government remains committed to preserving tribal languages, oral traditions and cultural heritage as a vital part of India’s civilisational identity. Many tribal languages and dialects survive primarily through oral tradition, making systematic documentation, technology-enabled revitalisation and the creation of dedicated spaces such as tribal and Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums an urgent national priority. It is one of the many steps in the journey towards
Viksit Bharat@2047.
The Conclave is being organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in collaboration with the Karnataka State Tribal Research Institute (KSTRI), Government of Karnataka, and the Central Institute of Indian Languages. Nearly 150+ participants across State took part in the National Conclave.
Karnataka Primers Released
In a special release ceremony, the Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, together with KSTRI, released Karnataka Primers in tribal languages — the Primer of Jenukuruba for Class 1 (Kannada, Maths, EVS), along with Sannivesha, Pragiti Nota, Thattegalu flashcards.
MoU signed between MoTA & CIIL
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs and CIIL signed a
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on language documentation and corpus development
, under which CIIL will support and share data with the Ministry on tribal languages.
Full-fledged Adi Vaani Platform, AI Bot Released
The session also saw the launch of “
Jago
”, the
official AI conversational assistant
of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, along with its mascot. Jago is designed to make information on tribal welfare schemes, programmes, initiatives and repositories easier to find, understand and access, bringing together trusted information from the Ministry through one intelligent interface.
The major highlight of the Conclave was the
launch of the upgraded Adi Vaani platform
, with new features including its new iOS application, the addition of five new languages, and the launch of the Adi Vaani logo.
In her welcome address, Smt. Kanagavalli, IAS, Secretary, Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, highlighted the urgent need for collective dialogue on tribal languages, stressing that the loss of a language also results in the loss of the culture and traditions associated with it.
Delivering the CIIL institutional address, Prof. Basavaraja Kodagunti, Director, Central Institute of Indian Languages, said that languages are living evidence of history and carry the knowledge and experiences of communities across generations. He highlighted the rich and ancient cultural heritage of tribal communities and stressed the need for field-level documentation, use of modern technology, and greater involvement of tribal youth in preserving tribal languages.
In his opening remarks, Shri Anant Prakash Pandey, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, said the preservation of tribal languages and heritage is an important component of the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, and that development should be rooted in dignity, knowledge and community-led interventions.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Member of Parliament, Mysuru Constituency, highlighted the contribution of tribal communities in preserving core Indic traditions through their languages and oral traditions. He further called for expanding the reach of the PM-JANMAN initiative to a larger number of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, and stressed the importance of mainstreaming tribal products through stronger market linkages.
Addressing the inaugural session, Shri Durga Das Uikey, Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs, said the biggest objective is to bring tribal communities into the mainstream on an equal footing, and that various initiatives are being continuously undertaken towards this goal. He also highlighted the presence and contribution of tribal communities in historical narratives, including references to tribal communities.
The session also highlighted the importance of celebrating and documenting the historical legacy of tribal communities, including the legacy of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.
Technical Sessions
Following a presentation by Shri Ganesh Nagarajan , Deputy Secretary, MoTA setting the tone for the day’s deliberations, the afternoon featured three panel discussions.
The first panel, on
Documentation, Endangerment & Community-Led Revitalisation
, examined the current state of tribal language documentation and community-driven revival models. Panellists included Dr R. Karthick Narayanan, Executive Director, CoDin; Amalesh Gope, Assistant Professor, Tezpur University; Chaithra Puttaswamy, Associate Professor, Department of Humanities and Social Sciences, IIT Kanpur; and Dr Sujoy Sarkar, Lecturer-cum-Junior Research Officer, CIIL.
The second panel, on
Technology Meets Tribal Languages
, mapped available technical tools — including automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, machine translation, corpus building, and keyboards and fonts — for tribal-language documentation, and discussed data protection, risk of misuse and safeguards for tribal linguistic knowledge, including questions around commercialisation of tribal-language data and content. The session included a live translation demonstration using audio recorded at the morning registration booth. Panellists included Dr Narayan Kumar Choudhary, CIIL Mysore; Prof. A.R.D. Prasad, Former Head, DRTC, ISI Bengaluru; Prof. Dileep A.D., IIT Dharwad; Dr Ritesh Kumar, CEO, UnRealTece; and Ranjani Prasad, Program Coordinator, Keystone Foundation.
The third panel, on
Multilingual Education for Tribal Students: Pedagogy, Content & Outcomes
, discussed tribal-language pedagogy and curriculum for tribal Schools, content-development gaps measured, availability of primers, dictionaries and teacher handbooks, and the link between tribal-language proficiency and livelihood outcomes. Panellists included Prof. Basavaraja Kodagunti, Director, CIIL; Prof. Minati Panda, JNU; Dr Ramanujam Meganathan, NCERT; and Arunabh Konwar, LLF.
Four Tribal Research Institutes — from Kerala, Odisha, Sikkim and Jharkhand — made presentations on their best practices in language preservation and ongoing projects.
The Conclave will continue on 25 August 2026 with a panel discussion on what tribal communities want, the adoption and signing of the Mysuru Declaration, and a series of sessions on Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums (TFFM).

title: UPI: Transforming India's Payment Landscape
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 AUG 2026 2:19PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Towards a Unified Payment Ecosystem
India's digital payments ecosystem has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past decade. It is driven by the vision of creating a simple and secure payment system accessible to every citizen.
The Unified Payments Interface (UPI),
developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s digital payments revolution. Today,
UPI is accepted in 11 countries
, with Greece and the Maldives being the latest to adopt India's real-time payment platform.
UPI and its Evolution
With
interoperable design and ease of use,
UPI has fundamentally changed the way individuals, businesses and government entities transact.
Real-time payment system
that powers multiple bank accounts through a single mobile application of any participating bank or payment service provider.
Integrates multiple banking services, fund transfers and merchant payments on a single platform.
Enables
round-the-clock
digital payments.
Uses
two-factor authentication
and end-to-end encryption to enhance transaction security.
Over the past decade,
UPI
has evolved into the backbone of India's digital payments ecosystem. Following are some of the key milestones in the evolution of UPI:
2016
UPI was launched
on a pilot basis in April 2016 with 21 member banks.
In August 2016, it was
rolled out to the public
as participating banks made their UPI-enabled mobile applications available on the Google Play Store.
The
BHIM
application was launched in December 2016 to enable digital payments using UPI. It allows users to make direct bank-to-bank transactions through mobile devices.
2017
Dynamic QR, a retail merchant platform enabling UPI payments via dynamic QR codes was launched, which dynamically included transaction specifics like payee info and exact totals, removing manual amount entry.
2018
UPI 2.0
was introduced with enhanced features to make digital payments simpler, more secure and seamless.
Invoice in the Inbox
allows users to view bills or invoices before authorising payments.
Signed Intent and QR
enables simplifies payment authorisation while maintaining security.
UPI Mandates
enables recurring payments through pre-authorised instructions.
Overdraft account linking
allows users to make UPI transactions using their overdraft accounts.
2019
SEBI allowed retail individual investors to use
UPI as an alternative payment mechanism
when applying for IPOs through designated intermediaries.
UPI crossed the milestone of
one billion transactions in a month
in October 2019, reflecting rapid nationwide adoption.
2020-2022
UPI AutoPay
was launched to support recurring e-mandates for subscriptions, utility bills, insurance premiums, SIPs and EMIs.
Feature phone users
were brought into the digital payments’ ecosystem through the launch of
UPI 123PAY
.  It allows transactions through interactive voice response (IVR) number, app-based functionality, missed calls-based approach and proximity sound-based payments.
UPI Lite
was introduced to enable low-value transactions in a faster and PIN-less manner.
The integration of
credit cards
with UPI further expanded digital payment options for users.
During FY 2021-22, UPI processed transactions worth over US$1 trillion and crossed
5 billion monthly transactions
in March 2022.
It also expanded internationally with its launch in
Bhutan
, marking its first cross-border deployment.
2023
Credit Line on UPI
was introduced, allowing pre-sanctioned bank credit lines to be linked as a funding account.
UPI accounted for
~70% of India's digital payment transactions
during FY 2023–24.
2024
UPI Circle
was introduced, enabling primary users to authorise secondary users with predefined transaction limits on the primary user’s bank account.
RBI enhanced the
UPI transaction limit for tax payments
from
₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh
per transaction. Higher limits also apply to select categories, including capital markets, IPO subscriptions, loan collections, insurance, healthcare and education.
The per-transaction limit for
UPI 123Pay
was raised to
₹10,000
, expanding its range of use cases.
The
UPI Lite
wallet limit was increased to
₹5,000
, with the per-transaction limit raised to
₹1,000
.
2025
On-device authentication for UPI
was introduced, enabling payments through smartphone fingerprint or face unlock.
Aadhaar-based Face Authentication
simplified UPI PIN onboarding, especially for first-time users, senior citizens and those without easy access to cards.
UPI Today
UPI has witnessed
unprecedented growth in both transaction volume and value
, reflecting its widespread adoption by individuals, businesses and financial institutions.
From FY 2016-17 to FY 2025-26:
Annual transaction volume
increased from
2 crore transactions
to
over 24,162 crore transactions
. It represents
~12,000-fold increase
.
Annual transaction value
grew from
₹0.07 lakh crore
to
~₹314 lakh crore
, recording more than
4,000-fold increase
.
UPI has transformed the scale and reach of digital payments in India.
In July 2026:
The UPI ecosystem comprises
741 live banks
, reflecting its widespread adoption across India's banking sector.
UPI processed 2,365.8 crore transactions
; and
Total
transaction value stood at ₹29.87 lakh crore.
UPI's Global Footprint
UPI has emerged as a leading real-time payment system globally.
As of 2024, UPI accounted for ~49% of global real-time payment transaction volume
. This achievement was highlighted by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in its “Growing Retail Digital Payments: The Value of Interoperability” report, published in June 2025.
UPI’s Global Footprint Continues to Expand
UPI is operational in
Bhutan, Nepal, Singapore, the UAE, France, Sri Lanka, Mauritius and Qatar
, enabling seamless cross-border digital payments.
In
June 2026
, NPCI International Payments Limited partnered with
ACLEDA Bank Plc.
to launch
UPI acceptance in Cambodia
, further strengthening India’s cross-border digital payment connectivity
In June 2026, UPI went Live in
Greece
for Cross Border Remittances, where eligible customers can transfer money instantly, securely, and seamlessly between Greece – India (through Eurobank).
On 30th July 2026, Cross Border Remittances between the
Maldives
Instant Payment System, ‘Favara’, and India’s UPI went live, marking a transformative milestone in cross-border digital financial connectivity and bilateral economic cooperation between the Maldives and India.
As on date, UPI is live in 11 foreign countries for UPI Acceptance and/or Cross Border Remittances.
A Decade of Digital Transformation
UPI has transformed the way India transacts by making digital payments simple, secure and interoperable. Its rapid adoption, continuous innovation and expanding global presence have made
UPI a key component of India's Digital Public Infrastructure
.

title: Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers chairs CEO Roundtable to discuss priorities to transform India into a Global Chemical Manufacturing and Innovation hub
subtitle: Government and Industry representatives Deliberate on roadmap for India’s USD 1 Trillion Chemicals Economy by 2040
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 AUG 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, in partnership with Invest India
,
convened a high-level CEO Roundtable today to deliberate on India’s ambition of building a USD 1 trillion Chemicals sector by 2040.
Chaired by Honourable Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J.P. Nadda in the presence of Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel,   the roundtable:
“India’s Chemicals Sector: Charting the Path to USD 1 Trillion by 2040,”
deliberated on the strategic priorities required to transform India into a globally competitive chemicals manufacturing and innovation hub. The roundtable was attended by more than 100 delegates from chemical industry from across the globe representing both foreign and domestic industry such as BASF, Tronox, Exxonmobil, Fujifilm, Lubrizol, Dow Chemicals, UPL, Reliance, DCM Shriram, HMEL, SABIC, Haldia Petrochemicals amongst others.
Representatives from more than 30 leading global and Indian chemical companies across speciality chemicals, petrochemicals and bulk chemicals participated in the discussions.
During the interaction, industry leaders highlighted several issues critical to the long-term competitiveness and growth of the sector, including:
Facilitation of large-scale investments through appropriate financing and investment-support mechanisms, particularly for capital-intensive upstream projects.
Upgradation of existing PCPIRs from industrial zones into major chemical manufacturing hubs which means upgrading infrastructure facilities and utilities for the industry.
Adopting Trade remedial measures to provide level playing field to ensure protection against unfair trade practices.
Greater support for R&D, innovation and technology development, through following measures :
To attract global talents from abroad, special tax breaks may be offered as done in countries like China, Japan and UK.
A Sovereign Fund may be formed to facilitate technology acquisition on the lines of S. Korea and USA.
Time-bound single-window clearances for chemical and petrochemical projects, particularly given that the multiple Central and State-level approvals involved in setting up such projects.
Development of a comprehensive National Feedstock Policy to reduce vulnerability to geopolitical and global supply-chain disruptions.
Addressing the gathering, the
Hon’ble Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers
Sh. Nadda emphasised that the sector has to touch USD 1 trillion vision by 2040 in the country.  He said the Government is committed to establishing a continuous and institutionalised dialogue mechanism with industry, with the objective of identifying impediments and translating suggestions into time-bound action. It would require sustained investment, technology development, stronger domestic manufacturing capabilities. He further stated that under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government continues to focus on creating an enabling ecosystem for investment, innovation, sustainability and long-term growth. The roundtable provided an important platform for engaging with industry leaders, understanding their priorities and discussing measures to further strengthen India’s position as a globally competitive chemicals manufacturing and innovation hub. He also assured that issues raised by the industry are duly noted and shall be suitably taken up relevant stakeholder Ministries.
In her address, Smt. Anupriya Patel, Union Minister of State
of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers, mentioned
that recent reforms and schemes launched by the Government to promote manufacturing across the sectors including Chemical and Petrochemical sector such as Bhavya Rasayan, Coal Gasification, Rare Earth Corridors, Critical Mineral Mission, reforms including Tax reforms, Labour reforms. She assured that industry that the Government is committed
to transition from a regulatory facilitator to an active growth partner, reducing administrative burden and ensuring the long-term viability of investments.
Stressing the importance of government and industry partnership,
Shri Tejveer Singh, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
, stated that the Chemicals sector offers major opportunities across given the expanding domestic demand across key downstream sectors. He emphasized the Department's commitment to collaborating closely with industry leaders to shape future policy interventions. On behalf of the Ministry, he also responded to the questions from the industry leaders.
Speaking on the occasion,
Ms. Nivruti Rai, MD & CEO, Invest India
mentioned that India is well positioned to emerge as a preferred global destination for chemicals manufacturing, supported by its large domestic market, skilled talent, improving infrastructure and ongoing reforms.
The roundtable also featured a presentation on global investment trends, foreign direct investment flows, state-level competitiveness and sector-specific opportunities.  Invest India also presented  the outcome of a survey conducted with the industry leaders which showed keen interest on part of the industry to come up with investments in the sector.
Apart from the above, representatives from State Governments of Odisha, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh also made interventions in the form of policy packages offered by respective State Governments to attract investment in the State.
The recommendations emerging from the consultation will inform future policy design, institutional reforms and investment facilitation framework that can be acted upon as a  ‘Whole of Government approach’ supporting India’s advancement towards becoming a globally competitive chemicals manufacturing and innovation hub.

title: CHEMCONNECT 2026: Industry-Academia Event will be held Tomorrow at IIT, MADRAS
subtitle: Technologies and Patents from the Centres of Excellence to be Showcased for Commercialization
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 AUG 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
CHEMCONNECT 2026,
a one-day Industry-Academia Event, will be held Tomorrow, at the Student Activity Centre (SAC) Hall, IIT Madras.
The event is jointly organized by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers and the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras in order to facilitate 18 CoE established by the Department.
The event is being organised by the Centre of Excellence in Biodegradable Packaging Materials (CoE BioPack), and Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Madras in collaboration with CIPET.
The event serves as an inventors-and-industry meet designed to facilitate direct dialogue without intermediaries. The event brings DCPC’s Centres of Excellence together with companies ready to commercialize innovations, offering a structured platform for industry leaders, start-ups, MSMEs, researchers, policymakers, incubators, and investors seeking strategic partnerships.
During the event, technologies, prototypes, and patents from Centres of Excellence established under the DCPC scheme "Setting up of Centres of Excellence (CoE) in the field of Chemicals and Petrochemicals" will be showcased.
Principal Investigators from CoEs will exhibit their work at dedicated stalls and interact directly with industry representatives to explore opportunities for collaboration, licensing, and technology transfer.
